root_causes.finding: canonicalCategory() accepts the requested canonical category before independent semantic validation; H.matches() may also use product.category as evidence.
root_causes.effect: An upstream wrong category can survive unchanged and appear valid.

root_causes.finding: Some matchers are much broader than the product class. Examples: women-shoes matches generic women terms; women-swim matches generic women; men-accessories matches generic men's/male terms.
root_causes.effect: A dress, phone case, bag or other item can satisfy the wrong category.

root_causes.finding: There is no hard negative/conflict pass that says a phone case cannot be evening wear, a pet bed cannot be plush toys, or a women's item cannot be men's-only when the title is explicit.
root_causes.effect: Positive keyword hits can override obvious product-type contradictions.

root_causes.finding: Routing lacks a canonical placement confidence/review state for ambiguous products.
root_causes.effect: Ambiguous products are forced into a shelf instead of TAXONOMY_REVIEW.

root_causes.finding: Matching uses title plus current category, so the category being tested can influence its own pass.
When several categories match, routing can resolve by taxonomy order rather than evidence strength.
root_causes.effect: Overlap such as dress/evening/skirt or home-decor/mirror can land inconsistently.

required_solution.name: HUNT Product Placement Gate V1
order: 1. Normalize supplier fields without trusting supplier/category placement.
2. Detect product_type from title + supplier taxonomy + structured attributes.
6. Score positive evidence independently from current category.
7. Require one clear winner above threshold.
9. Only after placement PASS run stock/shipping/profit gates.
10. Stylist may rank inside a passed shelf but may never change placement.
hard_rules: Current HUNT category is never positive evidence for its own validation.
Supplier category is a prior/evidence source, never sole authority.
Explicit product type outranks generic audience words.
Explicit gender contradiction blocks gender-only department placement unless product is clearly unisex.
A product may have one canonical department/category only.
No cross-category filler to improve shelf density.
Unknown/ambiguous routes stay out of canonical shelves until reviewed.
